summary: Chinese has no imperfect: ‘was doing’ and ‘used to do’ are built from words, around a verb that never changes. (1) Going on at a past moment: 在 / 正在 + verb, with a time or a …的时候 clause — 我回家的时候，爸爸在洗澡 ‘when I got home, Dad was in the shower’. (2) A lasting state: verb + 着 (zhe) — 门开着 ‘the door was open’, 他坐着等我 ‘he sat waiting for me’. (3) A habit, ‘used to’: a past frame — 以前, 小时候, 那时候 — with the plain verb, often with 常常, 总是 or 每天 — 小时候我常常去奶奶家 ‘as a child I used to go to Grandma’s’. None of these takes 了: they are the background, and only a completed event in the foreground does. ‘Wasn’t doing’ is 没在 + verb (他没在睡觉); ‘didn’t use to’ is 不 + verb in the past frame (以前我不喝咖啡); a change since then is 现在 … 了 (现在喝了).

head: What
How
Example
rows: 在 / 正在 + verb (+ a time or …的时候)
昨天晚上八点我在做饭。 At eight last night I was cooking.
我回家的时候，门开着。 When I got home, the door was open.
以前 / 小时候 / 那时候 + (常常 / 总是 / 每天) + verb
小时候我每天跟邻居的孩子玩。 As a child I played with the neighbours’ children every day.
blocks.caption: Ongoing and habitual: no tense, three tools

items.title: 在 + verb — an action in progress
points: 他在洗澡。 He is / was having a shower.
你来的时候，我正在睡觉。 When you came, I was asleep.

items.title: verb + 着 — a state that lasts
points: 门开着。 The door is / was open.
他坐着等我。 He sat waiting for me.

blocks.title: No 了 for the background
blocks.text: 了 reports a completed event. What was going on, and what used to happen, is background and takes no 了: 小时候我常常去奶奶家 (not *去了奶奶家). The event that happens against it takes 了: 我回家的时候，妈妈在做饭，她做了一个汤 ‘when I got home Mum was cooking — she made a soup’.

blocks.title: 着 zhe or 着 zháo?
blocks.text: 着 after a verb is the toneless zhe of a lasting state (开着, 坐着, 等着). 睡着 shuìzháo (C01) is another word, ‘to fall asleep’: 灯开着，可是他已经睡着了 ‘the light was on, but he had already fallen asleep’.

head: Frame
Meaning
Example
rows: 以前我不喝咖啡。 I didn’t use to drink coffee.
小时候我很喜欢玩玩具。 As a child I loved playing with toys.
那时候他在等我们。 At that time he was waiting for us.
我回家的时候，爸爸在洗澡。 When I got home, Dad was in the shower.
blocks.caption: Past frames: they stand first, and everything after them is in the past

blocks.title: Frames, not tenses
blocks.text: 以前, 小时候 and 那时候 stand before the verb or at the very start, and everything after them is understood as past: 小时候我每天走路去幼儿园 ‘as a child I walked to kindergarten every day’. 小时候 already means ‘when I was little’ — no …的时候 is added.

blocks.title: Then and now
blocks.text: A change from then to now: 以前 …，现在 … 了 — 以前我不喝咖啡，现在喝了 ‘I didn’t use to drink coffee; now I do’. The 了 marks the new situation.

blocks.title: Negating the background
blocks.text: ‘Wasn’t doing’ = 没在 + verb: 他没在睡觉. ‘Didn’t use to’ = 不 + verb in a past frame: 以前我不吃鱼. 没 + verb without 在 is ‘didn’t (do it at all, that time)’: 他没睡觉 ‘he didn’t sleep’.

blocks.title: Remembering and forgetting
blocks.text: 记得 + a clause recalls the past with no tense at all: 我记得小时候的幼儿园 ‘I remember the kindergarten of my childhood’. Forgetting is a completed change, so it takes 了: 我忘了 / 我忘记了 ‘I’ve forgotten’.

askYourself: Was the action going on at a moment (at eight, when I came home)? → 在 / 正在 + verb, no 了.
Is it a state that lasted (open, sitting, waiting)? → verb + 着.
Is it a habit of the past (used to)? → 以前 / 小时候 / 那时候 + (常常 / 总是 / 每天) + verb, no 了.
Is there a completed event in the foreground? → that one takes 了.
Negative? → 没在 + verb (wasn’t doing), 不 + verb (didn’t use to).
Is it 睡着 shuìzháo ‘fall asleep’, or a state with 着 zhe?
steps: Set the frame: a past time word or …的时候.
Choose: in progress (在), lasting state (着), habit (常常 / 每天).
Leave out 了 unless an event is completed.

traps: *小时候我常常去了奶奶家 → 小时候我常常去奶奶家.
*我回家的时候，爸爸洗澡了 (for ‘was showering’) → 爸爸在洗澡.
*门开了着 → 门开着 (it was open) / 门开了 (it opened).
*以前我没喝咖啡 (for ‘didn’t use to’) → 以前我不喝咖啡.
*我小时候的时候 → 我小时候.
他睡着了 (shuìzháo: fell asleep) ≠ 他在睡觉 (was sleeping).

quiz.q: ‘When I got home, Dad was in the shower.’
options: 我回家的时候，爸爸在洗澡。
我回家的时候，爸爸洗澡了。
我回家了的时候，爸爸洗澡。
quiz.answer: 我回家的时候，爸爸在洗澡。
quiz.why: What was going on takes 在 + verb; 洗澡了 would say he had his shower (done).

quiz.q: ‘As a child I often went to Grandma’s.’
options: 小时候我常常去奶奶家。
小时候我常常去了奶奶家。
我常常去奶奶家小时候。
quiz.answer: 小时候我常常去奶奶家。
quiz.why: A habit takes no 了, and the past frame comes first.
A lasting state is verb + 着, with no 了.
A past habit is negated with 不; 没喝 would be ‘didn’t drink it (that time)’.
睡着 zháo = fall asleep; ‘is sleeping’ is 在睡觉, ‘went to bed’ 睡觉了.
没在 + verb: an action that was not in progress.

notes.text: The Greek imperfect (έπαιζα ‘I was playing / I used to play’) holds both meanings in one verb form; Chinese splits them: 在玩 at a moment, 以前常常玩 as a habit.
The Russian imperfective past (играл) is both ‘was playing’ and ‘used to play’; Chinese uses 在 for the first and a past frame (以前, 小时候) with the bare verb for the second.
The imperfecto (jugaba) is both ‘was playing’ and ‘used to play’: estaba jugando ~ 在玩, solía jugar ~ 以前常常玩.
‘Was playing’ ~ 在玩 in a past frame; ‘used to play / would play’ ~ 以前 / 小时候 + 常常 + 玩 — no 了 and no change of the verb.
L’imparfait (je jouais) holds both meanings; être en train de ~ 在 / 正在, autrefois ~ 以前.

German has no aspect form: Präteritum or Perfekt with früher, damals (früher spielte ich oft …) and gerade (ich war gerade unter der Dusche); Chinese uses 以前 / 那时候 and 在 in the same way, around a bare verb.
Hindi has separate past forms: खेल रहा था ‘was playing’ ~ 在玩, खेलता था ‘used to play’ ~ 以前常常玩; Chinese builds both with words, not endings.
Persian mi- + past stem (bāzi mikardam) is both ‘I was playing’ and ‘I used to play’, and dāshtam bāzi mikardam is ‘I was in the middle of playing’ ~ 我在玩.
Arabic كَانَ + imperfect (كَانَ يَلْعَبُ ‘he used to play / he was playing’) does with an auxiliary what Chinese does with a frame word: 以前他常常玩 / 那时候他在玩.
Hebrew הָיָה + participle (הָיִיתִי מְשַׂחֵק ‘I used to play’) marks the habitual past; Chinese uses 以前 / 小时候 and the bare verb.
Turkish -iyordu ‘was …-ing’ (oynuyordu) ~ 在玩 and -ardı ‘used to’ (oynardı) ~ 以前常常玩 — suffixes where Chinese uses words.
Japanese 遊んでいた ‘was playing’ ~ 在玩, よく遊んだ ‘often played’ ~ 以前常常玩; -ている also gives states, like 着: ドアが開いている ~ 门开着.
Korean 놀고 있었어요 ‘was playing’ ~ 在玩, 놀곤 했어요 ‘used to play’ ~ 以前常常玩; 문이 열려 있었어요 ‘the door was open’ ~ 门开着.
Finnish uses the same past for both (leikin ‘I played / was playing’), with olin leikkimässä for ‘I was in the middle of playing’ ~ 我在玩.
Swahili nilikuwa ninacheza ‘I was playing’ uses kuwa ‘to be’ in the past + a present form — close to Chinese 在 + verb in a past frame.
Vietnamese is close: đang ~ 在 (lúc đó tôi đang ăn ~ 那时候我在吃饭), hồi nhỏ ~ 小时候, hay / thường ~ 常常 — no tense anywhere.
Polysynthetic languages tend to put ‘ongoing’ and ‘habitual’ into suffixes inside one long verb word; Chinese uses separate words (在, 着, 常常) around a verb that never changes.

seeAlso.note: German has no special form: the Präteritum of common verbs or the Perfekt with früher / damals (früher spielte ich oft), and gerade for ‘in progress’; Chinese uses 以前 / 小时候 and 在 / 着.
Arabic كَانَ + imperfect (كَانَ يَلْعَبُ ‘he used to play / was playing’); Chinese: 以前常常玩 / 那时候在玩.
Hebrew past of הָיָה + participle (הָיִיתִי מְשַׂחֵק ‘I used to play’); Chinese: 以前 / 小时候 + bare verb.
在 / 正在 for ‘in progress’ came in S14; 着 is new here.
